key_insight: The paper shows that an AI system can act like an autonomous X-ray scientist, using large language models to align single crystals at a real synchrotron beamline without constant human intervention. This demonstrates closed-loop, adaptive experimentation at a large scientific facility.
problem_solved: Traditional synchrotron experiments require expert operators to repeatedly inspect results, adjust alignment, and guide the next step. This work addresses the challenge of automating that expert decision-making in a high-precision experimental environment.
method: Uses an agentic AI workflow powered by large language models to plan and adapt experimental actions.
Autonomously aligns single crystals at a synchrotron beamline by interpreting feedback from the instrument.
Runs in a closed loop, where the AI observes outcomes, decides the next action, and refines the procedure in real time.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this is a strong example of LLMs moving beyond text generation into embodied scientific control systems. It highlights how agentic AI can accelerate discovery by reducing manual labor and enabling adaptive experiments in real-world infrastructure.

paper_title: An agentic artificially intelligent X-ray scientist
paper_authors: Zhantao Chen, Alexander N. Petsch, Aidan J. Israelski, Rajan Plumley, Lingjia Shen
